item.title: Global Lacrosse Games roster breakdown: Canada women
item.description: Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women’s lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest lacrosse players in history, like the legendary Dana Dobbie. We are bound to see more greatness from this squad that has a No. 1 ranking in mind to chase after. The roster Canada has put together for the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games is an exciting mixture of seasoned leaders and exploding stars. Let’s break it down. Field Players Erica Evans Annabel Child Jordan Dean Milana Zizakovic Kassidy Morris Aurora Cordingley Maggie Cuddy Nicole Perroni Megan Kinna Madalyn Baxter Kylea Dobson Goalies Kameron Halsall Alecia Nicholas One word to describe this roster is… Poised. This Canadian team is primed and prepped for a big tournament. They have battled to the very end against USA the last few times the rival nations have matched up in a Sixes Championship, and are likely itching to get over that hump. Players like Erica Evans , Megan Kinna, Nicole Perroni and Aurora Cordingley have played on these big stages in a Canadian uniform before. Evans brings a decade of familiarity alone, playing with the Canadian national team since 2015. Their experience from playing for Canada for many years will bring a level of poise and comfort to the Global Lacrosse Games that’s needed to thrive and win against the other top nations in the world. Biggest star: Erica Evans Evans is coming off a championship summer with the Maryland Charm and has been an international star since she won a gold medal with the U19 Canadian team. She started off a historic run by being named to that 2015 All-World Team and has since been an All-World selection in nearly every international event she has participated in – in all disciplines: field, Sixes and box. She is a strong lefty and dominant force in the middle of the field, sparking transition plays and coming up with big caused turnovers. Her offensive IQ is next-level; she executes two-player games seamlessly and constantly opens up scoring opportunities for herself and others. Evans will be the main all-around Canadian player to keep an eye on throughout each game. Breakout candidate: Kameron Halsall Halsall is the type of goalkeeper who can make or break the outcome of a game. She stands tall in the crease and is a strong-handed lefty who clears the ball quickly the moment she makes a save in order to provide scoring opportunities for her offense going the other way. She is one of the goalies who thrives in a Sixes setting due to substantial breakaway shot opportunities that result from the fast pace of games. item.description: Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in the summer from Paris Saint-Germain -Credit:Carl Recine, Getty Images Glen Johnson has addressed comments from France FIFA World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit, suggesting Liverpool overpaid for 'overrated' £123 million ($166.6 million) summer acquisition Bradley Barcola. The former Reds defender has expressed confidence that the winger will find his form following a challenging beginning to his Anfield tenure. Barcola toiled in an unaccustomed striker's position on Wednesday as Liverpool's flawless UEFA Champions League league phase record ended with a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahçe in Istanbul. The France international had shone in his prior Champions League road fixture, delivering an impressive hat-trick during the 6-3 winat LASK. -Credit:Laurence Griffiths, Getty Images However, those strikes represent the sole goals Barcola has managed across his 13 outings for the Reds following his blockbuster transfer from European champions Paris Saint-Germain on August 31. Earlier this month, former Arsenal, Barcelona, and Chelsea midfielder Petit, who captured the World Cup with France in 1998, stated via the Liverpool Echo : "£120m? I would never put that price tag on the table. We all know that in France. "We know that he is a quality player, he could sometimes be great, but he doesn't have consistency during games. He was good most of the time with Paris because of the whole team behind him. I would probably have spent £60m or £70m, maximum. That's my opinion. It's becoming common now that English clubs are spending so much money on overrated players." However, Johnson, who registered 200 appearances for Liverpool with nine goals and 13 assists following his £17.5 million (around $29 million) transfer from Portsmouth in June 2009, considers Barcola "world-class" and argues he shouldn't be evaluated solely on his price tag. He said: "I don't think Barcola is overrated. I think he's world-class. I've been a fan of his for a long time. I think he's brilliant. item.title: VfB Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen preview: Undav and Füllkrug in contrasting form ahead of Topspiel
item.description: VfB Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen preview: Undav and Füllkrug in contrasting form ahead of Topspiel Deniz Undav's VfB Stuttgart will host Niclas Füllkrug's Werder Bremen in the marquee fixture of matchday 10. VfB Stuttgart The captain's goal drought contributed to Stuttgart's slow start to the season. Undav had found the net twice, but none of those goals came in the league as his poor form led him to miss out on Jürgen Klopp's squad nomination for the second time. Meanwhile, Ermedin Demirović has been their go-to guy this season, although he was unable to score in the defeat against Galatasaray, who had an unsuccessful attempt to sign the Bosnian striker in the summer. Stuttgart returned to winning ways in Bundesliga on matchday 8 after successive defeats. Team News The absence of Atakan Karazor and Angelo Stiller in midfield would cause selection issues for Hoeneß, although the former has a slight chance to recover from an injury that forced his early substitution against Galatasaray. Demirović and Undav started together against both Leverkusen and the Turkish champions, although Hoeneß preferred different playing systems. In goal, Dennis Seimen is expected to return in place of the experienced Fabian Bredlow. Werder Bremen After matching Rudi Völler's club record of scoring in seven successive Bundesliga games, Füllkrug earned a national team call-up by Klopp on Thursday. The 33-year-old leads the scoring chart in Bundesliga, and he already opened a five-goal lead over a certain Harry Kane. The nine goals from the former Torjägerkanone winner helped Werder Bremen to start the matchday in fifth place after having to fight relegation consistently in past seasons. Daniel Thioune’s troops are unbeaten in Bundesliga since starting the campaign with a 4-1 defeat to Freiburg. Team News Mitchell Weiser suffered another injury setback inside the first 15 minutes in last week's 2-0 win over TSG Hoffenheim, and he'll miss this one at the very least. Eren Dinkci, who scored the second goal after replacing him, is expected to start in the right wing. Head-to-head Werder Bremen are unbeaten in their last two trips to Stuttgart, although the Swabians did win 4-0 at Weserstadion last season. The last time a game between the two sides ended goalless was in February 2006. Predicted Lineups Click here to see our predicted Stuttgart vs. Werder Bremen lineups.

item.title: Forget the schedule, Jalen Brunson has another theory to explain the NBA injury crisis
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Almost every team in the NBA has been hit by injuries this season. We are less than a month into the new campaign, and several big names have already been sidelined due to one issue or another. There are fears that the list could grow in the coming weeks and months. Many feel the schedule is the reason why, but Jalen Brunson has a different theory. Jalen Brunson says the NBA’s injury crisis could be down to ‘style of play’ It has been a real shame to see several fantastic players miss games due to injuries this season. From Anthony Edwards and Ja Morant to Paolo Banchero and Kawhi Leonard, many are currently sidelined, causing their respective teams to be significantly weaker. Several theories have been going around – from the gruelling schedule to a lack of preparation in pre-season practice sessions. But Jalen Brunson thinks it may actually be down to the style of play most coaches employ in the NBA in today’s game. When told that 16-20 per cent of the league is on the injury report, Brunson said on the Roommates Show : “I just feel like it’s a lot. “Is the schedule asking too much of the players? No! I mean, the schedule is the schedule. It’s been that way for – we’ve been playing 82 games for, I don’t know how many years – like decades. “But it’s obviously unfortunate things happen, but yeah, I don’t think it’s the scheduling part. I think maybe it’s like the style of play. We’re playing fast-paced basketball.” The intensity involved in almost every team sport in the world has gone up in recent years, and it is showing no signs of slowing down. That has definitely made games more interesting, but it has to be said that the physical burden on players has gone up as well. That increases the risk of injuries, which we are all seeing right now. item.description: JOHNSTON — Central Falls might have that magic. And Classical survived on grit. The Warriors were relentless for 80 minutes against Mt. Hope to continue their unexpected playoff run. A pair of goals from Daniel Rios Aceituno paced a 3-1 comeback in a Division II semifinal victory over the Huskies. Peter Breen closed out an unending night between Classical vs. Central in the second semifinal. The senior’s penalty kick lifted the Purple to a 0-0 (6-5) victory after eight penalty rounds on a breezy, Nov. 5 night at Johnston High School. Watch RI high school games on NFHS Network The eighth-ranked Huskies and third-ranked Purple advance to the championship at Rhode Island College on Sunday at 2:30 p.m. It’s the first title appearance for Central Falls, who are looking for their fifth championship overall, since it won a D-III crown in 2005. Classical advances to a title round for the first time since 2014 when it won a D-II championship. Central Falls won the season meeting against Classical, 4-1, in Providence in mid-September. “I told the team to keep our head up,” Rios Aceituno said. “Just keep it up and keep pushing. We've been working hard in practice every day.” “Right before I take that kick, I know what I'm going to do,” Breen said. “I feel calm. If the goalie guesses right, he guesses. But if he doesn't, that's awesome and we’re in the championship on Sunday.” Read on below for more on the D-II boys soccer semifinals. item.title: Worcestershire trio aim to make more Cup magic
item.description: It's now 55 seasons since non-league Hereford United's 2-1 fourth-round replay win over top-flight Newcastle United entered English football folklore as arguably the greatest FA Cup shock of all time. Elsewhere in the Midlands, though, there have been many other upsets and moments of cup magic too. Telford United (in 1984) and Kidderminster Harriers (in 1994) both made it to the fifth round, and Worcestershire village side Alvechurch hold a record they will keep forever - unless the rules are changed again - after taking four replays to see off Oxford City in a qualifying round tie in 1971. Worcester City were involved in a record-breaking penalty shootout against Scunthorpe in 2014 - the same year they famously beat Coventry City. But, while the memory of that day at Hereford - Ronnie Radford et al - surpasses all other memories, across the Worcestershire border, it perhaps still irks a bit. Accompanied by fallen 1970s non-league stars Stafford Rangers, Worcestershire clubs make up three of the four non-EFL Midlands sides to have made it through to the first round proper - the Harriers plus seventh-tier duo Alvechurch and Worcester, who all face EFL clubs. How will they fare this time? Plymouth Argyle v Alvechurch 5th in League One v 6th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier 7) On paper, it looks a very tall order for Alvechurch. But not every non-league club has got an FA Cup pedigree like the Church's manager Kyle Storer. The former Bedworth United, Tamworth, Hinckley United, Atherstone Town, Nuneaton Town, Kiddy Harriers, Wrexham, Cheltenham Town, Solihull Moors, Nuneaton Borough, AFC Telford United, Kettering Town and Alvechurch player is not just a walking advert for Midlands non-league football, he has got plenty of FA Cup "previous" to be taken into consideration. "I've been very fortunate," Storer told BBC Midlands Today. "I got to the fourth round with Kiddy Harriers, when we played at Sunderland in front of 40,000. And that was having beaten Peterborough over two games with a team that had Joe Lolley, Marvin Johnson and Chey Dunkley." And we got Norwich at home in third round the following year." Dion Dublin and Darren Huckerby both netted twice in a 4-1 win but Storer had the last word by getting one back. "It was voted goal of the round too," he grins. "I've had some amazing FA Cup runs but let's hope we can go and create another day to remember. Let's hope we can cause some damage. item.title: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick has unfinished business with Diego Simeone ahead of Atletico Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick has unfinished business with Diego Simeone ahead of Atletico Madrid clash The last few weeks have been terrible for Barcelona, starting with defeats to Real Madrid and PSG to the injury to star midfielder Rodri . But the Catalans will not let that hamper their form as they travel to the Metropolitano to face Atletico Madrid this weekend. After all, Barcelona are running the risk of losing out on the top spot in the La Liga table, if they succumb to a defeat at the hands of Atletico Madrid. Hansi Flick has unfinished business As reported by MARCA , beating Atleti and its coach Diego Simeone will be of particular importance for Hansi Flick, who has quite the history against Los Colchoneros . Flick and Simeone have quite the history between them. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) During his coaching career, Flick has crossed paths with Atletico Madrid 12 times. On paper, the record favours him a lot, with the Catalans leading on wins. Of those 12 meetings, 10 have come during Flick’s time at Barça, yielding six wins, one draw and three defeats. However, the stats do not tell the whole story as two of the three victories have come in a rather painful manner for Flick and his team. The scars of last season Both the defeats, in fact, came last season. The first came in the Copa Del Rey semifinal first leg, when Atletico Madrid secured an emphatic 4-0 win to leave Barcelona all but elminated. Although the Catalans made an admirable comeback in the second half, they were unable to completely overturn the sheer magnitude of the defeat. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona were defeated twice by Atletico last season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The second one was even more agonising for Hansi Flick. Simeone’s side won 2-0 in the first leg of the Champions League quarterfinal at the Camp Nou, a result Barcelona were unable to overturn at the Metropolitano. This effectively put an end to Barcelona’s hopes of winning the Champions League, much to the frustration of Flick. Now, that same Atletico Madrid side, who were defeated by Bayern Munich in the Champions League, will have the opportunity to dethrone Barcelona at the top of the table this weekend. Hansi Flick, though, clearly has unfinished business and won’t let them have it easy.

item.title: ‘It’s not right’ – Jason Kelce thinks one aspect of College Football ‘doesn’t make sense’
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jason Kelce enjoyed an incredible career in the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles, but not every player is so fortunate as to earn the kind of money the former centre did in their respective careers. The current college system was described by Kelce as ‘the Wild West’ in his latest New Heights podcast, where he was able to speak to legendary head coach Nick Saban about the current landscape in the world of College Football. The transfer portal has changed the landscape of the college scene, with colleges battling against each other financially in the race to sign specific players. It has brought into question just how committed players are to actually developing themselves, as opposed to simply chasing the highest-paying opportunity. Although Kelce is on the side of the players being granted the opportunity to earn from playing at the college level, he has also shared his concerns over the lack of commitment required from the players with the contracts they are signing. Jason Kelce does not agree with the current College Football contract situation Revenue sharing was introduced last year, which required the colleges to start compensating their student-athletes for their participation in the teams. Although there are certainly some positives to this, it is apparent that the system is far from perfect. “These kids sign contracts, but they mean nothing. They just leave. They don’t have any penalty for leaving,” Nick Saban said. https://open.spotify.com/embed?uri=spotify%3Aepisode%3A1h6N7H8Nm6nabFjSG6eijX “Well, that’s the thing that doesn’t make sense to me. Like, and I know you’ve talked to Congress and they’re trying to get this thing right, but it doesn’t make sense that there’s a commitment from the university, but no commitment in terms of like a contract or any type of time period from the player. Like it’s, you know, it’s the Wild West,” Jason Kelce responded. “It’s not right what’s going on. And it’s not in the best interest of the player, like you just said, like all for players getting paid. But, I developed so much of, you know, work ethic and all of these other attributes in college because you have to figure it out and you have to grind it. And it’d be interesting going through college nowadays, with how it happens and how quickly guys just up and leave the moment there’s any type of adversity or anything.” Kelce and Saban clearly have their concerns over the impact the financial games between colleges could have on the players’ characters as they develop towards a career in the NFL. item.title: 'We are an honest group' - Andoni Iraola reacts as Liverpool top the Premier League fouls chart before Crystal Palace trip
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LIVERPOOL-PRESSER - AFP Andoni Iraola has admitted Liverpool are "sometimes too honest" after a striking statistic showed no Premier League side have conceded more fouls this season. The Reds head to Crystal Palace on Sunday on the back of two straight defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and their manager wants a response, with Ryan Gravenberch still a doubt because of a heel problem. Liverpool top the Premier League for fouls conceded Liverpool have conceded 128 fouls in the Premier League this season, more than any other side in the division, as reported by The Independent. At the other end of the scale, only three teams have won fewer fouls than Iraola's side, who have been awarded just 88. The Reds have lost their last two games, against Arsenal and Fenerbahce, and were denied a penalty against the Gunners despite Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled. The topic was raised at Iraola's press conference ahead of Sunday's trip to Selhurst Park. Iraola unsure how to take referee's praise The Liverpool boss accepted that his players do not try to con officials, and revealed that their conduct had even earned praise from the referee. "We are quite an honest group, sometimes too honest," Iraola said. "Even the other day after the game, the referee congratulated us… I'm not sure if I like that or not! "Our behaviour was very good. I think it has to be genuine; you cannot fake things; it has to be genuine complaints. We are willing, we want to press, we want to be intense – but the balance is that there's a big difference." Iraola explains Liverpool's 'strange season' Liverpool sit fifth in the Premier League, nine points off leaders Arsenal. They have conceded only nine goals in nine league games, but have already let in 10 in four Champions League matches. "It's been a strange season," Iraola added. "In the Champions League, we are scoring a lot and conceding a lot. In the Premier League, we are scoring less and conceding less. We obviously want to score more, concede less! "It's a matter of controlling the games. Sometimes against Fenerbahce, we're controlling too much, having good positions and arriving but sometimes we have to throw numbers in the box. It will take away more control, yes, but it gives us more threat. Especially against Arsenal… the way we attack the box has to be better." Gravenberch a doubt as Liverpool chase Palace win Iraola confirmed that Gravenberch is touch and go for Selhurst Park as the midfielder continues to manage pain in his heel. "A week ago, we were on a run and in a good place and in a better mood," he said. "Now it changes and it has to be like this. We have to react after two defeats: we need the win against Palace away."

item.description: Alabama heads into another hostile environment on Saturday afternoon as they travel to Tiger Stadium to take on a fellow two-loss squad in LSU. item.title: Bottas Reveals What Broke in His Mexico Crash, and Why Cadillac Didn’t See It Coming
item.description: Valtteri Bottas says heat from his Cadillac’s brakes caused the suspension failure that sent him into the barriers at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Bottas was braking for Turn 1 at the end of the main straight when his front-left suspension failed, and the car spun backward into the tire barrier. He climbed out on his own, and the race was red-flagged so the barrier could be repaired. Speaking to the media at Interlagos on Thursday, Bottas gave the fullest account yet of what went wrong. He also talked about his future at Cadillac, which Darshan covered here . Brake Heat Reached the Wishbones The part that failed was the mountings for the wishbones, the suspension arms that connect the wheel to the chassis. Bottas said the team has found exactly what broke and why. “These things shouldn’t happen. But again, it happened,” he said. “The main thing is we understand why. We did have certain limits when it comes to temperatures, but we’ve had to review those.” The heat came from the brakes, which are hard to cool in Mexico City’s thin, high-altitude air. “Still, the heat from the brakes, it’s got to go somewhere. And at the moment, part of it is going to the wishbones,” Bottas said. The team knew the parts got hot, but not that hot for that long. “We’re just running too long time in the red zone,” he said. “We thought it was safe, but we never tested by running it so long at that temperature.” He added that his car was running hotter than expected in Mexico, so he was already lifting and coasting to manage it when the suspension broke. What Cadillac Has Changed for Brazil Cadillac has gone back to the previous version of the wishbone mountings and lowered the temperature limits for those parts. “We’ve changed the spec to actually previous spec,” Bottas said. “It’s just the wishbone mountings. And we’ve lowered the limits, which shouldn’t be an issue here.” The suspension is now back at Silverstone, where Cadillac is stress testing it to set more accurate temperature limits. Bottas doesn’t expect a repeat at Interlagos, where Sunday should be much cooler, with maybe some rain. “If we didn’t understand what broke and why, then you would struggle with confidence. But we understand, and we know now what the limits are. So that’s why it’s okay,” he said. “Mexico is going to be the hardest one for the rest of the season with the temperatures.” The crash left him with only a bruised muscle, and he said he now feels “completely normal.” Valtteri Bottas (FIN) Cadillac Formula 1 Team MAC-26, practice day at the Mexico City Grand Prix, Oct. 30, 2026. item.description: Goalkeeper considers early retirement after Jesús de Miguel's death Goalkeeper Jesús Owono, 25, is reportedly considering retiring from professional football following the tragic collision involving Jesús de Miguel. The Bears (6-2) are winners of three in a row after they traveled to the Pacific Northwest and defeated the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in one of the best regular season victories in recent memory. Quarterback Caleb Williams was able to move the ball unlike previous quarterbacks against Seattle's defense, while running back D'Andre Swift capitalized with three rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a debut that will be remembered for years to come as he stifled the Seahawks offense for much of the game. As for the Buccaneers (3-5), they have climbed their way out of the NFC South basement and are back on tracking following the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield. Tampa has won three of their last four games and is coming off a historic 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons, where they didn't complete a single pass in monsoon conditions. Despite their poor record, the Buccaneers have a formidable defense, and their offense can get things going with their impressive ground attack. Here are five Buccaneers players we'll be watching this Sunday night: 1. QB Baker Mayfield It's been two weeks since Baker Mayfield returned to action following an injury to his right hand, and he hasn't had to do a whole lot. During Tampa Bay's two-game winning streak, Mayfield has completed just seven of 14 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. He made history last week by not completing a single pass in the Buccaneers' win over the Falcons, which is a nice soft restart to his season. Don't expect that to be the case Sunday, though. The Bears' defense will be too good to allow Tampa to solely rely on their rushing attack to carry the load. Mayfield will likely have his most passing attempts since late September against a Bears defense that can suddenly now get after the quarterback more effectively. We'll see how healed his thumb is and whether or not he can get after this Bears secondary that has a proponent for giving up big passing plays. 2. RB Bucky Irving If the Bears are going to stifle the Buccaneers offense, they need to contain running back Bucky Irving. And this is a homecoming Irving is likely looking forward to. The 2024 fourth-round pick out of Hazel Crest is playing in his first game in Chicago since turning pro, and he's coming off a career day. Irving totaled 170 rushing yards on 27 carries last week and scored a touchdown in Tampa's win over Atlanta. The rushing yards and carries were both career highs, and it was Irving's third game in four weeks with over 100 rushing yards. He is the engine that is powering the Buccaneers' offense and will be the focal point that the defense needs to hone in on.
